title: 0. How to use this document
body:
This document defines the shared system for Hudson AI's websites and web products, together with the documentation site that explains it. It is an executable spec to use before the actual site is built — not a report that implementation or deployment is complete. It borrows the information structure and example-driven learning style of the Toss TDS Mobile docs, and applies the UX judgment principles and AI delegation principles from the attached images to the web.

Non-developers set direction with sections 1–4, designers design screens with sections 5–10, and developers and AI implement with sections 11–16. If a value or component is missing, don't add one arbitrarily; follow the change process in section 14. Before release, pass the acceptance criteria in section 15.

The confirmed scope is responsive web. iOS and Android-only APIs, native font-scaling mappings and a mobile app's bottom tab bar are not part of the default structure. Mobile browsers are supported as the narrow-screen condition of the same web. The default theme follows the system setting between light and dark and can be switched in the header (`?theme=dark` also opens it). The charcoal media workspace is provided as a separate inverse scope. Document languages are Korean and English, switched in the header or with `?lang=en`.

title: 1. Purpose and intent
body:
**People define the important decisions, and AI selects and composes verified tokens and components to build a consistent web.**

Hudson's impression is accuracy, clarity and working speed. White and warm gray form the information structure, charcoal carries text and media, and #FD4D20 reveals the next action and the brand's energy. Bright orange is not repeated on every title, icon and border, which would blur priorities.

The system has three groups of users. Designers look for the reason to apply something and visual exceptions; developers look for API, state and accessibility contracts; and AI reads the allowed choices and review conditions. So every documentation page must contain an explanation, a working example and a machine-readable spec together.

Example product features are project creation, file upload, speaker separation, translation and dubbing jobs, subtitle review and live language settings. These are examples to validate UI patterns, and must not be taken as actual supported features, accuracy, latency or pricing. Use only verified product data for figures and product promises.

title: 2. Standards for improving references for the web
body:
| Reference element | Application in Hudson web | Execution rule |
|---|---|---|
| Docs split into foundations and components | Foundations → Components → Patterns → AI Kit | Generate URLs and the navigation menu from the same manifest |
| Abstracted Typography tokens | Web type tokens with role names | Use tokens like heading-xl and body-md; no arbitrary px |
| Table for various native zoom levels | Handle browser zoom, default font changes and reflow | Check rem, unitless line-height, and 200%/400% zoom |
| Single mobile task flow | 3 columns for docs; 2–3 regions for product lists and editors | On small screens, rearrange the priority of the same information |
| BottomCTA, BottomSheet, etc. | ActionBar, Dialog and Inspector within the work area | Place key CTAs close to context; fix to the bottom only when needed |
| Touch-centered states | Add hover, focus-visible, keyboard and selected states | Never expose a function through hover alone |
| Simple lists | Web data tables, filters, search and multi-select | Provide a state contract for sorting, paging and bulk actions |
| Describing how components look | Document intent, API, async behavior and failure recovery | Apply the same doc template to every component |

Borrow the structure and learning style, but don't use Toss's brand, copy, assets, dedicated packages or private components as they are. Prefer rules that are executable in Hudson over visual similarity.

title: 3. Turning UX laws into working rules
body:
We apply Hick, Fitts, Jakob, Proximity and Von Restorff, as confirmed in the attached material, as follows. The counts and spacings below are Hudson's initial design baselines, not absolute figures of the laws themselves. They may change with user validation.

| Principle | Question to ask in screen design | Execution rule | How to verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hick | What choices must be decided now? | Show the core action first and fold advanced options. Provide search and recents for long language lists | Observe whether people can explain their next action on first entry |
| Fitts | Is the important control easy to reach? | Regular buttons have a minimum height of 40px; touch and primary CTAs 44px. Icons get a real click area | Reachable and selectable with keyboard, pointer and touch |
| Jakob | Does it match web conventions people already know? | The logo goes to the start page, links navigate, buttons act. Search is Cmd/Ctrl+K and Esc closes popups | People can do it without being taught a new interaction |
| Proximity | What belongs to the same group? | 8–16px inside a group, 24–32px between groups. Bind label, field, description and error in the same Field | Check the grouping is still visible with borders removed |
| Von Restorff | What is the single most important thing right now? | One solid primary per work area, in principle. Distinguish the whole screen from row and modal contexts | Check for competing CTAs and unneeded orange surfaces |

Don't delete choices indiscriminately. Preserve rarely used settings with progressive disclosure. A top button on the web isn't always bad either. Judge together its closeness to the work area, what it covers, pointer travel and scrolling conditions.

Design review order: user goal → most important information → next action → required states → groups and spacing → visual finish. Don't decide decoration first and fit the purpose around it.

title: 4. Docs site information architecture and layout
body:
### 4.1 Navigation structure

| Menu | Pages | Representative URL |
|---|---|---|
| Overview | System introduction, quick start, design principles | /overview, /getting-started |
| Foundations | Color, Typography, Spacing, Layout, Radius, Elevation, Motion, Iconography | /foundations/typography |
| Components | Button, Link, Field, TextInput, Select, Combobox, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Tabs, Badge, Alert, Toast, Tooltip, Dialog, Drawer, Table, Pagination, Skeleton, Progress | /components/button |
| Patterns | DocsShell, ProductShell, Upload, AsyncJob, MediaWorkspace, LiveSession, EmptyState, ErrorRecovery | /patterns/async-job |
| Content & A11y | Terminology and writing rules, internationalization, accessibility | /guidelines/accessibility |
| AI Kit | ScreenBrief, token manifest, component registry, delegation prompts, review | /ai-kit |
| Governance | Versions, change history, contribution, deprecated items | /changelog |

The home page consists of a one-line statement, search, hub tiles for the main categories, an AI Kit introduction, the palette ratio and frequently viewed docs. Hubs and documents are all generated from the same route manifest.

### 4.2 Docs screens

- Top Global nav: 64px tall, logo · 5 main categories (Foundations · Components · Patterns · Guides · AI Kit) · search. Translucent background and a 1px bottom divider. The skip link appears on the first Tab.
- Sub-menus are not placed in the navigation bar. Each main category has a hub page (/foundations, /components, /patterns, /guides) whose body shows documents as cards, filtered with category chips.
- Document pages: a 48px sticky Local nav below the Global nav (page title + section links + delegation button). There is no left navigation or right table of contents.
- Body container max 72rem, side margins 32px at 1024px and above · 24px at 768–1023px · 16px below 768px. Below 1024px the main categories move to a menu button and Drawer, and the Local nav links scroll horizontally.
- Page bottom: previous and next docs within the same category, and a sitemap footer listing all docs.
- Body descriptions are max 68ch; examples and API tables may use the full body width. The top of sticky regions adds the header height and a spacing token.
- Use aria-current on the current main category and aria-current="location" on the current section in the Local nav. So sticky regions don't cover focus, set scroll-padding-top to the sum of both bars' heights.
- Direct URL entry, reload, back and hash links all work. Share an example's selected state via URL query when needed.

### 4.3 Common template for every page

Breadcrumb → title · one-sentence purpose · status (Stable/Beta/Deprecated) → when to use/avoid → live example → rules and anatomy → states → API table → accessibility, responsive and internationalization → wrong usage → code → AI contract → change history.

The Preview / Code / Specification tabs show the same data and examples. Code copy reports success and failure, and Specification provides JSON download and copy. An example with no external service is labeled "Demo data". Never create fake downloads or fake API successes that look like they run.

The Typography page includes Korean/English/mixed sample text, a table of size, line height, weight and CSS tokens by role, a narrow-screen toggle, and examples of long titles and 200% text zoom. The accessibility demo toggles don't replace browser zoom for the whole site.

title: 5. Color system
body:
### 5.1 Primitive

The orange ramp fixes #FD4D20 (500); darker steps (600–900) rotate the OKLCH hue toward warm gray (35°→50°), and lighter steps (50–400) rotate toward peach. Lowering lightness at the same hue reads as brick or red and clashes with warm gray. Success, warning and error status colors are also taken only from this palette (orange, charcoal, warm gray, white); no color outside the palette — green, yellow, red — is used anywhere. The build checks this hue rule, that status colors stay inside the palette, and the light and dark contrast pairs.

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| orange-50 | #FEF5EE | Lightest brand background |
| orange-100 | #FFE9DB | Selected-state background |
| orange-200 | #FED4BE | Light accent border |
| orange-300 | #FFB392 | Illustration · chart support |
| orange-400 | #FE8B64 | Illustration · chart support |
| orange-500 | #FD4D20 | Fixed brand accent · primary action |
| orange-600 | #E8480B | Primary action hover (4.62:1 with charcoal text) |
| orange-700 | #B34202 | Small brand text · pressed (5.68:1 on white) |
| orange-800 | #8B3901 | Dark accent text |
| orange-900 | #662D03 | Darkest accent |
| warm-0 | #FFFFFF | Default surface |
| warm-50 | #FAF9F6 | Overall document background |
| warm-100 | #F5F3EF | Inset · hover surface |
| warm-200 | #E7E3DC | Decorative divider |
| warm-300 | #D2CCC3 | Disabled border |
| warm-500 | #78716C | Limited secondary text |
| warm-600 | #625B54 | Default secondary text |
| warm-700 | #4A443E | Borders on inverse and dark; neutral strength |
| warm-800 | #35312C | Dark inset surface (added for dark mode) |
| warm-900 | #282521 | Inverse and dark surface |
| warm-950 | #171614 | Primary text · charcoal |

### 5.2 Semantic

| Semantic token | Light value | Dark value |
|---|---|---|
| bg.canvas | warm-50 | warm-950 |
| bg.surface | warm-0 | warm-900 |
| bg.subtle | warm-100 | warm-800 |
| bg.inverse | warm-950 | warm-100 |
| text.primary | warm-950 | warm-50 |
| text.secondary | warm-600 | warm-300 |
| text.muted | warm-600 | warm-300 |
| text.inverse | warm-0 | warm-950 |
| text.brand | orange-700 | orange-400 |
| border.subtle | warm-200 | warm-700 |
| border.control | warm-500 | warm-500 |
| field.bg | warm-100 | warm-800 |
| field.border | warm-200 | warm-700 |
| field.border.hover | warm-300 | warm-600 |
| action.primary.bg | orange-500 | orange-500 |
| action.primary.hover | orange-600 | orange-400 |
| action.primary.pressed | orange-700 | orange-300 |
| action.primary.fg | warm-950 | warm-950 |
| action.primary.pressed.fg | warm-0 | warm-950 |
| action.selected.bg | orange-100 | orange-900 |
| action.selected.fg | orange-700 | orange-300 |
| focus.ring | warm-950 | warm-50 |
| status.success | warm-950 (surface warm-0, border warm-700) | warm-50 (surface warm-900, border warm-300) |
| status.warning | orange-800 (surface orange-50, border orange-200) | orange-300 (surface orange-900, border orange-700) |
| status.danger | orange-700 (surface orange-100, border orange-500) | orange-400 (surface orange-900, border orange-500) |

The usage ratio by screen area starts at base (warm-0·50) 60%, structure (warm-100–600) 25%, charcoal (warm-900·950) 12% and accent (orange) 3%. Orange is used only for one primary action per screen and for selected states. This ratio is recorded in colorRatio in tokens.json.

Color is referenced in three stages: primitive → semantic → component. Screen files don't use HEX directly. Status colors (status.success · warning · danger) reference only orange, charcoal and warm-gray tokens, as in the table above. They are told apart not by hue but by icon shape, text and fill strength (success is charcoal, warning is a light orange surface with an outline, error is a strong orange surface or fill). Status is always shown together with text and an icon. Text input fields use field.bg (light warm gray) and field.border (a light border), and the focus ring stays charcoal. Dark mode reconnects the semantic tokens under [data-theme="dark"], and the build checks the same contrast pairs (4.5:1 for regular text) in both light and dark.

### 5.3 Contrast and forbidden combinations

Contrast calculated with the WCAG relative luminance formula: #FD4D20 / #FFFFFF ≈ 3.36:1, #FD4D20 / #171614 ≈ 5.39:1, #E8480B / #171614 ≈ 4.62:1, #B34202 / #FFFFFF ≈ 5.68:1. The baseline is at least 4.5:1 for regular text and 3:1 for large text. Large text is roughly 24 CSS px or larger, or bold text of 18.67px or larger.

So don't make a bright orange button with small white text the default. The default is charcoal text. A variant that must use white text is provided on an orange-700 background with a separate component token. #78716C is about 4.798:1 on white but about 4.329:1 on #F5F3EF, so don't use it unconditionally on every surface. For required input borders and icons, check 3:1 against the actual adjacent background, and don't reuse a weak divider as an input border. Check hover, pressed, selected, transparency and inverse combinations individually too.

title: 6. Typography
body:
For the default font, obtain Pretendard Variable from an official distribution and self-host it with its license. Fallbacks: system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif. Code: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Consolas, monospace. Don't make loading from an external font CDN mandatory. Use font-display: swap and check for layout shift caused by the fallback.

| Role | Default font-size | line-height | weight | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| display | clamp(2.5rem, 1.5rem + 3vw, 4rem) | 1.1 | 700 | Marketing hero only |
| heading-xl | 3rem / 2.25rem on narrow screens | 1.15 | 700 | Document H1 |
| heading-lg | 2.25rem / 1.75rem on narrow screens | 1.2 | 700 | Section H2 |
| heading-md | 1.5rem | 1.35 | 600 | H3 |
| heading-sm | 1.25rem | 1.4 | 600 | Panel · card title |
| body-lg | 1.125rem | 1.6 | 400 | Intro description |
| body-md | 1rem | 1.6 | 400 | Body · input |
| body-sm | .875rem | 1.5 | 400 | Table · description |
| label-md | .875rem | 1.4 | 600 | Button · label |
| caption | .8125rem | 1.5 | 400 | Metadata |
| code | .875rem | 1.6 | 400 | Code · token |

Keep html font-size at 100% and don't apply a 62.5% reset. The table values assume a 16px root and don't override user settings. Use -0.02em letter spacing on headings only, and the default letter spacing of 0 for body text. Korean uses word-break: keep-all + overflow-wrap: anywhere to handle long URLs and the like. Avoid all-uppercase and justified paragraphs.

Separate the text role from the HTML meaning. A small visual title can logically be an H2. A screen has one main H1 and a consistent heading order. Don't shrink must-read descriptions and errors to 11–12px. Numbers in tables use tabular-nums and provide units and column headings. If you truncate, provide an accessible way to see the full value.

Avoid fixed-height text boxes. Build buttons with min-height so they can wrap. Headings, buttons and labels must not be cut off at 200% text zoom and 400% browser zoom. A clamp-based display must also pass the zoom check.

title: 7. Spacing·Radius·Elevation·Layout
body:
| System | Allowed values | Selection criteria |
|---|---|---|
| spacing | 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96px | Icon–label 8, inside a field 12, card 24, section 48–64 |
| radius | 0, 4, 8, 12, 16px, full | Code 4, inputs and buttons 8, cards 12, modals 16, avatars and status dots full |
| elevation-0 | none | Regular docs cards and panels |
| elevation-1 | 0 2px 8px rgb(23 22 20 / .08) | Small floating elements |
| elevation-2 | 0 8px 24px rgb(23 22 20 / .12) | Menus and popovers |
| elevation-3 | 0 16px 48px rgb(23 22 20 / .18) | Modals |
| z-index | base 0, sticky 100, dropdown 200, modal 300, toast 400, tooltip 500 | Don't cover layers with an arbitrary 9999 |

Don't put a shadow on every large card. Build the default hierarchy with background, lines and spacing. A 1px border and a 2px focus outline with a 2px offset are allowed. These line widths, and font and icon sizes, are exceptions to the spacing scale. Icons are 16, 20 and 24px; the real click area follows the component size.

ProductShell starts with a 64px Header, a 240px Nav, the work Main and, when needed, a 320px Inspector. Below 1280px the Inspector turns into a Drawer, and below 1024px the Nav collapses. If an editor needs a minimum supported width, record it separately in the Pattern contract. Don't lock the default docs site to desktop only.

Use the 12-column grid for wide marketing layouts, and CSS Grid with a fixed navigation width for regular docs. Don't force every screen into 12 columns. Internal rearrangement of reusable cards and panels can be handled with container queries, recorded separately from the viewport breakpoints and their purpose.

title: 8. Component contracts
9. Hudson domain patterns
body:
### Upload

Provide a large Dropzone together with a "Choose file" button. Take supported formats and the maximum size from product settings and show them before selection. Validate on the server as well. Show per-file progress, cancel and retry, plus a completed list. Never make it work by drag alone. Do not trust the client file name or MIME type to decide server processing.

### MediaWorkspace

The media Preview is a charcoal inverse area, the Timeline is the working area, the Transcript is the text-review area, and the Inspector is the area for the selected speaker and language settings. Do not distinguish speakers by color alone; use a name or number as well. Give the waveform canvas a non-visual alternative and DOM-based playback and seek controls. Autoplay with sound is prohibited by default. Provide a shortcut list and rules for avoiding conflicts.

### AsyncJob

Separate the progress stage from the completion rate. If the backend does not provide a percent, show an indeterminate progress bar and stage text such as "Translating". Never advance to 99% arbitrarily. If there is an estimate, state that it is an estimate. Stop polling in a terminal state and refresh when the user returns to the tab. Retries must account for idempotency and for duplicate billing or duplicate job creation. Do not promise free retries without an actual policy.

### LiveSession

Provide connection status, language, how latency and quality are measured, the last update time, and recovery actions. The word "live" alone does not guarantee a connection. Distinguish dropped → reconnecting → recovered or failed, and show the scope of impact the user needs to check. Do not convey connection status with a single color dot.

### Table·EmptyState·ErrorRecovery

The default density is comfortable (row min-height 48px), with an optional compact (40px). Row height grows to fit long content and enlarged text. Do not overlap selection, row navigation and the menu button. Do not treat empty data, no search results, insufficient permission and a network failure as the same screen. For retryable failures, provide a retry button and keep the user's input and selection. For hard-to-recover actions such as deletion or ending a session, provide a confirmation Dialog that states the impact.

title: 10. Motion·Content·Accessibility·Internationalization
body:
Motion duration: instant 0ms, fast 120ms, standard 180ms, slow 240ms. The default easing is cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1). Rely mainly on color, opacity and transform, and avoid repeating motion that shakes the layout. Under prefers-reduced-motion, remove movement, scaling and repetition but keep state communication. Do not hide informational progress.

Make copy specific about the verb and the object: "Create project" rather than "OK", and "We couldn't finish uploading the file. Check your network and try again." rather than "Failed". If the real cause is not confirmed, do not guess and state it as fact. A button's promise of completion must match the task state.

The accessibility target is WCAG 2.2 AA. Review full keyboard operation, visible focus, focus not hidden by sticky areas, skip links, semantic landmarks, name/role/value, status announcements, screen magnification, and information conveyed by more than color. The 44px target size is Hudson's recommended default. The WCAG 2.5.8 AA minimum is 24×24 CSS px or the stated spacing and exception conditions; do not confuse the two criteria.

The document starts with lang="ko" and applies the appropriate lang to English-only regions. Libraries must allow strings to be injected from outside. Handle time, numbers and currency with the Intl API and an explicit timezone. Never show a date as just "10/11". Review the condition where text grows 50% longer, and mixed Korean and English. Prefer logical properties such as margin-inline in layout to prepare for RTL.

title: 11. Implementation structure
body:
The recommended initial stack is React + TypeScript + Vite, CSS custom properties + CSS Modules, MDX docs, React Router, Storybook, Vitest + Testing Library, and Playwright + axe-core. This is the project's proposed stack; do not assume it is already installed. If an existing repository exists, its stack and versions take priority. For a new project, check dependency versions against official documentation and supported ranges at implementation time and pin them in the lockfile. A docs site that needs no backend defaults to a static build.

```text
packages/tokens/      source JSON, validation, generated CSS·TS
packages/ui/          shared components, types, stories, behavior tests
packages/contracts/   ScreenBrief·ComponentContract JSON Schema
apps/docs/           docs routes, MDX, search, playground
apps/examples/       Hudson pattern examples
tests/e2e/           keyboard·routing·zoom·responsive review
```

The paths above are a proposed structure. If the actual repository is a single app, keep src/tokens, src/components, src/docs and so on, but preserve the same separation of responsibilities. The UI package never imports the docs app. Use only public exports, and do not import internal implementation paths directly in screens.

Use the token JSON as the single source and generate CSS, TS and docs tables in the build. Validate semantic alias existence, circular references, types and color-contrast pairs. Generate the props table, search index and AI manifest from the component registry so hand-written docs and code never drift apart.

Search covers statically generated document titles, descriptions, keywords and token names. Use client-side search suited to the data size, and show the document name and location in each result. Provide no-result, loading and keyboard navigation. Cmd/Ctrl+K must account for input conflicts. Selecting a result navigates to the real route and moves focus to the page heading.

Highlight code blocks at build time and never run dynamic code with eval. The Playground only adjusts pre-registered examples and allowed props. The clipboard feature handles HTTPS and browser permission failures and provides a manual-selection fallback.

Security: do not put secrets, real uploaded data or personal information in the example bundle. Build MDX only from trusted repository content and do not run arbitrary user HTML. If you connect a real upload or API demo, design authentication, authorization, rate limits, server validation and retention policy separately. Do not leave original files or sensitive content in demo logs.

title: 12. Token and responsive CSS starter example
13. The spec AI reads
body:
### 13.1 ScreenBrief input form

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "1.0.0",
  "systemVersion": "1.0.0",
  "screenId": "docs.typography",
  "purpose": "Choose and apply typography tokens by role",
  "audience": ["designer", "developer", "ai"],
  "primaryAction": {"label": "Copy spec", "actionId": "copy-spec"},
  "secondaryActions": ["copy-code", "change-preview-locale"],
  "layout": "DocsShell",
  "density": "comfortable",
  "theme": "light",
  "contentPriority": ["purpose", "preview", "tokens", "rules", "api"],
  "requiredStates": ["ready", "search-empty", "copy-success", "copy-error"],
  "dataSource": "static-registry",
  "responsivePolicy": "docs-default",
  "acceptanceCriteria": ["keyboard-complete", "no-page-overflow", "contrast-aa"]
}
```

The JSON above is an illustrative example. To make it executable, declare required fields, enums, whether additional properties are allowed, and schemaVersion validation in the JSON Schema, and run the validator in CI. An actionId must exist in the real event handler registry. A product-screen Brief adds the data model, permissions, state transitions and API failure policy.

### 13.2 ComponentContract required fields

id, version, status, purpose, useWhen, avoidWhen, props, variants, stateAxes, statePrecedence, tokenBindings, keyboardBehavior, accessibility, responsiveBehavior, i18nBehavior, events, examples, acceptanceCriteria, deprecatedReplacement.

Each prop records its name, type, default, required flag and description. Token bindings record which CSS property in which state connects to which semantic token. allowedComponents and allowedTokens are generated from the actual exports and token data, and the build verifies that every reference in every example is valid.

### 13.3 Implementation instruction to pass along as-is

> Implement Hudson AI Web Design System v1.0. First check the repository structure, AGENTS.md and dependencies, and keep the existing tech stack. Based on this spec and tokens/registry/ScreenBrief, build DocsShell, Foundations, Components, Patterns and AI Kit. Refer to the Toss docs' navigation, explanation and example structure, and apply Hudson's #FD4D20, charcoal, warm-gray and white tokens. Do not use a mobile app's native zoom rules or a bottom tab bar by default. Choose every component from existing exports and semantic tokens. Make search, routing, copy, state transitions and keyboard operation actually work. Mark examples without data as demos. Do not add colors, spacing, radii, shadows or new components on your own. Resolve missing requirements through the spec's change procedure and record the reason. Generate docs and API from the same source, and after implementation check the acceptance criteria in section 15. In the result, record changed files, commands run, verification results and open items.

### 13.4 AI selection order

1. Confirm the purpose, user, primaryAction, data and permissions.
2. Choose a Layout from existing Patterns.
3. Choose existing Components, variants and states.
4. Bind semantic tokens.
5. Implement responsive behavior, keyboard, async, failure and long text.
6. Review the actual screen and the contract.
7. If something needed is missing, record the gap and add it to the registry with the smallest change.

What AI may change freely: copy that fits the real product data, selection of allowed tokens and variants, and combinations of existing patterns. What needs change review: new tokens, public API, new patterns, accessibility behavior and destructive-action policy. Do not change the whole system for the look of a single screen.

title: 14. Versions·Maintenance·Exceptions
body:
Show the same system version on tokens, components and docs. Use patch for bug fixes, minor for compatible additions, and major for breaking changes such as removing tokens or changing APIs. Deprecated items provide a replacement and a migration example and record a removal date.

Change procedure: write the usage scenario and why the existing system cannot solve it → write the smallest addition and its impact → update tokens/registry/schema → update examples, tests and docs → review and change history. AI writes reviewable changes first and follows the repository's review policy. Exceptions record exceptionId, reason, scope, owner and reviewDate. Never hide arbitrary inline styles or HEX values under the name of an exception.

Definition of done: a working implementation, state examples, docs, contracts, accessibility and responsive review, and a change history all exist together. A result with only design screens and no connected buttons or routing is not considered done.

title: 15. Acceptance criteria and tests
body:
| Area | Pass criteria | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| Routes | Direct entry, reload, back and hash links work; a nonexistent path returns 404 | E2E |
| Search | Cmd/Ctrl+K, keyboard navigation, result navigation, no-result and Esc handling | E2E + manual |
| Copy | Success over HTTPS and failure on permission denial are announced; manual fallback | Browser test |
| Tokens | No unknown references or alias cycles; no on-screen HEX or arbitrary spacing | schema + lint |
| Contrast | Text 4.5:1, large text 3:1, informational UI adjacent contrast 3:1 | Calculation + axe + visual check |
| Responsive | No page-level horizontal scroll at 360/768/1024/1440/1920px | Playwright viewport |
| Zoom | No loss of information or tasks at 200% text zoom and 400% browser zoom | Manual review in a real browser |
| Keyboard | Every task possible; focus order, return and Esc work; focus not obscured | Manual keyboard + E2E |
| Components | Check specified states, long labels, invalid+focus, and re-run during loading | stories + behavior tests |
| Tables | Sorting, selection, empty results and failure handling; independent scroll on narrow screens | E2E |
| Async | Failure, cancel, retry and duplicate prevention; no fake progress | mock API integration tests |
| Docs | Props, examples and JSON match the real registry | Build verification |
| i18n | No clipping with mixed Korean and English, 50% text expansion or long URLs | fixtures + visual check |
| Motion | No repetition or large movement under reduced-motion; state information kept | Media setting test |
| Security | No secrets, sensitive data, eval or arbitrary HTML execution | Code review |

400% zoom includes, for example, an effective width of about 320 CSS px in a 1280px-wide window. Regions that need a two-dimensional structure, such as data tables, timelines and code, may scroll horizontally on their own, but headings, descriptions and primary actions must reflow. Do not report full accessibility as passed merely because automated axe passes.

Initial performance budget: aim for 200KB or less of compressed JS on the default docs entry, and load large playground and syntax features on demand. Set size and loading policies for fonts and images. The Core Web Vitals targets, judged at the 75th percentile of real-user data split by mobile and desktop, are LCP ≤2.5s, INP ≤200ms and CLS ≤0.1; if there is no real-user data, report only lab results with the measurement conditions stated. Adjust the performance budget after checking the project environment.

State supported browsers as the two latest stable versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari at implementation time, plus mobile Safari and Chrome. Check support for specific CSS, clipboard and dialog behavior at implementation time.

title: 16. Implementation order and delivery scope
body:
1. System foundation: tokens JSON·CSS·TS, schema, color contrast, typography·spacing·radius.
2. Docs skeleton: DocsShell, route manifest, real search, headings, table of contents, hashes and 404.
3. Representative pages: Typography and Color, preview, code and spec copy, responsive.
4. Core components: Button, Field, Input, Combobox, Tabs, Dialog, Alert, Table, Progress.
5. Hudson patterns: Upload, AsyncJob, MediaWorkspace, LiveSession. Reproduce as demos without a real service.
6. AI Kit: ScreenBrief form, JSON Schema, registry, delegation instruction and review-checklist download.
7. Quality review: keyboard, zoom, states, failure, long text, version and change history.

The final delivery includes the runnable docs web source, generated tokens, component public API, types and schema, demo data, tests, README run instructions and change history. State backend integration and public deployment as separate scope. Do not report the whole system as complete just because the first stage is done.
